claims.text: InMemoryEventStore.Append adds the events to the order's stream and to the all list; ReadAll(position) returns every order's events from all in append order, skipping the first position of them.
OrderProjection.CatchUp applies each event from store.ReadAll(Position) and increments Position after each; Position has a private setter, changed only by CatchUp and Rebuild.
Rebuild calls Clear(), sets Position to 0, then calls CatchUp(store), replaying every event in the store.
Nothing in EventSourcedOrder or InMemoryEventStore calls a projection; projections only read from the store and record no event.

OrderStatusCounts keeps each order's current status (statusOfOrder); Apply decrements that status's count (removing it at 0) and increments the new status's count; StatusAfter maps OrderPlaced to new, OrderPaid to paid, OrderShipped to shipped, OrderCancelled to cancelled.
OrderTimeline.Apply adds a line '<status> at HH:mm' to the order's list in Lines.

Rebuild_GivesTheSameCountsAsTheLiveProjection: live catches up, order 1 is shipped and saved, live catches up again; a new OrderStatusCounts rebuilt from the store has equal Counts and equal Position.
StoreWithThreeOrders places orders 1 to 3 and pays order 1 before saving; At is a fixed DateTimeOffset field of the test class, passed to every Place/Pay/Ship/Cancel call in it.

RecordOrderStatusHistory adds one order_status_history row per domain event Order records; the events are not kept anywhere; orders placed before stage-3 have only the placed row the AddOrderStatusHistory migration wrote from orders.placed_at.

While the events are kept, a projection's data need not be protected like the events: if it is lost or an Apply bug is fixed, rebuilding from the events restores it.
